claim: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.
source: Lung cancer (LC) is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and introduction with citation support (Ferlay et al., 2021)

claim: Traditional therapeutic approaches such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy have provided only a marginal improvement in the treatment of lung carcinomas.
source: Traditional therapeutic approaches such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy have provided only a marginal improvement in the treatment of lung carcinomas.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a general assessment of traditional therapies

claim: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common lung cancer subtype, accounting for 85% of cases.
source: Inhibitors targeting specific genetic aberrations present in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the most common subtype (85%), have improved the prognostic outlook
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with percentage provided

claim: Only a fraction of NSCLC patients benefit from targeted molecular therapies due to the complexity of the LC mutational spectrum.
source: but due to the complexity of the LC mutational spectrum, only a fraction of patients benefit from these targeted molecular therapies.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a limitation of targeted therapies

claim: Macrophages are one of the most abundant leukocyte infiltrates in NSCLC.
source: In NSCLC, one of the most abundant leukocyte infiltrates is macrophages.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: Macrophages can have a pivotal role in early NSCLC establishment, malignant progression, and tumor invasion.
source: These highly plastic phagocytes, which are part of the cellular repertoire of the innate immunity, can have a pivotal role in early NSCLC establishment, malignant progression, and tumor invasion.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a summary of macrophage roles

claim: Emerging macrophage-targeting therapies have been focused on re-differentiation of macrophages toward an antitumorigenic phenotype, depletion of tumor-promoting macrophage subtypes, or combination therapies.
source: Emerging macrophage-targeting therapies have been focused on the re-differentiation of the macrophages toward an antitumorigenic phenotype, depletion of tumor-promoting macrophage subtypes, or combination therapies combining traditional cytotoxic treatments with immunotherapeutic agents.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as current therapeutic approaches

claim: 3D platforms, including organoid models, are advancing tools to study immune cell-epithelial cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment.
source: 3D platforms, including organoid models, are quickly advancing powerful tools to study immune cell-epithelial cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as an emerging technology

claim: Co-cultures of immune cells with NSCLC organoids allow for in vitro observation of tumor microenvironment dynamics closely resembling in vivo settings.
source: Co-cultures of immune cells along with NSCLC organoids allow for an in vitro observation of the tumor microenvironment dynamics closely resembling in vivo settings.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a capability of co-culture systems

claim: Average survival for lung cancer is less than 5 years post-diagnosis.
source: Lung cancer (LC) is the leading cause of cancer-associated death worldwide with an average survival being less than 5 years' post-diagnosis (Ferlay et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Mortality due to lung cancer surpasses the combined mortalities caused by breast, colon, and prostate malignancies.
source: Mortality due to LC surpasses the combined mortalities caused by breast, colon, and prostate malignancies (Howlader, 2020).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) encompasses about 15% of all lung cancer cases.
source: The two primary histological LC types are small cell lung cancer (SCLC), encompassing about 15% of all cases
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support (Conway et al., 2016; Li et al., 2020)

claim: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for about 85% of lung cancer cases.
source: and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the predominant subtype accounting for about 85% of cases (Conway et al., 2016; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) accounts for approximately 40% of NSCLC cases.
source: Further sub-division of NSCLC includes lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD, ~40%)
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support (Arora et al., 2021)

claim: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) accounts for approximately 25% of NSCLC cases.
source: lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC, ~25%)
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support (Arora et al., 2021)

claim: Large cell carcinoma accounts for approximately 10% of NSCLC cases.
source: and large cell carcinoma (~10%) (Arora et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: More than 80% of lung cancer patients receive their diagnosis at advanced stages of the disease, which makes surgical treatment difficult.
source: While surgical tumor resection has the greatest success therapeutically, the vast majority of patients (more than 80%) receive their diagnosis at the advanced stages of the disease, which makes surgical treatment difficult (Conway et al., 2016; Ettinger et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Platinum-based chemotherapy and radiotherapy are used as the first line of treatment for advanced lung cancer cases.
source: In these cases, platinum-based chemotherapy and radiotherapy are used as the first line of treatment.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as standard treatment approach

claim: The therapeutic effects of traditional chemotherapy and radiotherapy approaches are often modest and provide great discomfort to patients due to their inherent toxicity.
source: However, the therapeutic effects of these traditional approaches are often modest and provide great discomfort to the patients due to their inherent toxicity (Conway et al., 2016; Kong et al., 2021; Sarode et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Targeted therapies using small molecule inhibitors such as gefitinib or erlotinib have been developed to exploit LC-specific mutations.
source: With the recent but rapid advancement of next-generation sequencing methods, targeted therapies using small molecule inhibitors such as gefitinib or erlotinib (epidermal growth factor receptor [EGFR] tyrosine kinase inhibitors), among others, have been developed to exploit LC-specific mutations (Dearden et al., 2013; Chung, 2016).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Targeted therapy improved response rates compared to traditional treatments but its utility has been limited to a fraction of LC cases due to the complexity of the LC mutational landscape.
source: When compared to the traditional treatments, targeted therapy improved response rates but its utility has been limited to a fraction of LC cases, largely due to the complexity of the LC mutational landscape.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a limitation of targeted therapy

claim: The eventual acquisition of resistance of the tumor to targeted therapies has hindered the improvement in survival rates, maintaining the average 5-year survival at around 18%.
source: The eventual acquisition of resistance of the tumor to targeted therapies has further hindered the improvement in survival rates, maintaining the average 5-year survival at around 18% (Conway et al., 2016; Kong et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: The involvement of the immune tumor microenvironment has been highlighted as an emerging hallmark involved in multiple cancer types.
source: The involvement of the immune TME has even been highlighted as an emerging hallmark involved in multiple cancer types (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: The specific composition of the immune microenvironment surrounding the tumor can affect the prognosis, disease progression, and patient survival.
source: The specific composition of the immune microenvironment surrounding the tumor can affect the prognosis, disease progression, and patient survival (Arora et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Therapies aimed at modulating the immune microenvironment were long believed to be ineffective in LC as a limited response was observed with non-specific treatments using interleukin 2 (IL-2) or interferon (IFN).
source: Therapies aimed at modulating the immune microenvironment were long believed to be ineffective in LC as a limited response was observed with non-specific treatments (using interleukin 2 [IL-2] or interferon [IFN]).
evidence: Stated in the introduction as historical context

claim: The immunogenicity of LC became known following trials using immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated protein-4 and antiprogrammed cell death protein-1 (PD-1).
source: The immunogenicity of LC only became known following trials using immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated protein-4 and antiprogrammed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) (Rizvi et al., 2015; Lynch et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: The range of LC responses to immunotherapies remains variable, depending mostly on the mutational burden of the tumor and the subsequent neoantigen diversity.
source: The range of LC responses to immunotherapies remains variable, depending mostly on the mutational burden of the tumor and the subsequent neoantigen diversity which, together with a range of other factors (such as programmed death-ligand 1 [PD-L1] expression, interferon-γ [IFN-γ] signaling, and others) determine T cell reactivity against them (Schumacher and Schreiber, 2015; Hendriks et al., 2018; Hegde and Chen, 2020).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: The changing mutational landscape of the lung tumor in response to therapies along with evasion of immune surveillance often lead to the acquisition of chemoresistance.
source: Additionally, the changing mutational landscape of the lung tumor in response to these therapies along with evasion of immune surveillance often lead to the acquisition of chemoresistance (Kong et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: Macrophages are the predominant cell type within the immune infiltrate in lung tumors.
source: In particular, macrophages – phagocytic cells of the innate immunity – have garnered interest as the predominant cell type within the immune infiltrate in lung tumors.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a key observation

claim: Macrophages are highly diverse and feature many phenotypes with different properties and functions.
source: Macrophages are highly diverse and feature many phenotypes with different properties and functions.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a characteristic of macrophages

claim: The general presence of macrophages within the immune infiltrate in cancer is mostly indicative of a negative prognosis, but their effect on cancer progression appears subtype-dependent.
source: While their general presence within the immune infiltrate in cancer is mostly indicative of a negative prognosis, their effect on cancer progression appears subtype-dependent (Conway et al., 2016; Sarode et al., 2020; Cassetta and Pollard, 2018).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with citation support

claim: LUAD lesions feature a particularly high abundance of macrophages compared to other NSCLC subtypes.
source: One of the most highly represented leukocyte types within the LC TME are macrophages, with LUAD lesions featuring a particularly high abundance of these cells compared to other subtypes (Conway et al., 2016; Cassetta and Pollard, 2018; Kargl et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support

claim: Macrophages are either monocyte-derived and originate from the bone marrow or tissue-resident and originate from embryonic tissues such as fetal liver and the yolk sac.
source: They are either monocyte-derived and originate from the bone marrow or tissue-resident and originate from embryonic tissues such as fetal liver and the yolk sac.
evidence: Stated in section I as a description of macrophage origins

claim: Macrophages settle into their respective niches in successive waves during embryogenesis and further development.
source: As such, they likely settle into their respective niches in successive waves during embryogenesis and further development.
evidence: Stated in section I as a developmental process

claim: Macrophages take on a tissue-specific identity which determines their transcriptional profile and specialization depending on the anatomical site of settling.
source: Depending on the anatomical site of settling they take on a tissue-specific identity which determines their transcriptional profile and specialization (Sreejit et al., 2020; Laviron and Boissonnas, 2019; Ginhoux and Guilliams, 2016; Blériot et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support

claim: Macrophages feature phenotypic plasticity brought on by specific tissue-dependent microenvironmental cues such as metabolite composition, the nature of phagocytosed particles, or the cellular constituents within the niche.
source: Macrophages feature incredible phenotypic plasticity brought on by the specific tissue-dependent microenvironmental cues such as metabolite composition, the nature of phagocytosed particles, or the cellular constituents within the niche.
evidence: Stated in section I with reference to Figure 1A

claim: After receiving specific environmental stimuli, macrophages polarize and change the expression of their surface markers as well as alter their effector functions.
source: After they receive specific environmental stimuli, they polarize and change the expression of their surface markers as well as alter their effector functions (Figure 1A; Aras and Zaidi, 2017; Sreejit et al., 2020; Rodero et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support and reference to Figure 1A

claim: The classical binary division of macrophages includes M1 (classically activated by IFN-γ and/or lipopolysaccharides) and M2 (alternatively activated by IL-4, IL-10, IL-13, transforming growth factor β, and/or glucocorticoids) cells.
source: The nomenclature for these opposing macrophage phenotypes was not established until the 2000s when their distinct metabolic profiles were identified, and they have been henceforth referred to as M1 (classically activated by IFN-γ and/or lipopolysaccharides [LPS]) and M2 (alternatively activated by IL-4, IL-10, IL-13, transforming growth factor β [TGF-β], and/or glucocorticoids) cells (Figure 1A; Conway et al., 2016; Arora et al., 2021; Chávez-Galán et al., 2015; Mills et al., 2000; Murray et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support and reference to Figure 1A

claim: The M1 phenotype is characterized by high expression of interleukin 1β (IL-1β), IL-6, tumor necrosis factor alfa (TNFα), as well as inducible nitric oxide synthase.
source: The M1 phenotype is characterized by high expression of interleukin 1β (IL-1β), IL-6, tumor necrosis factor alfa (TNFα), as well as inducible nitric oxide synthase.
evidence: Stated in section I as a characteristic of M1 macrophages

claim: M2 macrophages are unique for their high expression of arginase which blocks nitric oxide production through urea and ornithine synthesis.
source: Conversely, the M2 macrophages are unique for their high expression of arginase which blocks nitric oxide production through urea and ornithine synthesis.
evidence: Stated in section I as a characteristic of M2 macrophages

claim: M2 macrophages express high levels of IL-10 and TGF-β, cytokines with antiinflammatory functions.
source: They also express high levels of IL-10 and TGF-β, cytokines with antiinflammatory functions (Arora et al., 2021; Bissonnette et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support

claim: M1 macrophages are generally antitumorigenic due to the secretion of primarily pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: Due to the secretion of primarily pro-inflammatory cytokines, M1 macrophages are generally antitumorigenic

claim: M2 macrophages seem to promote tumorigenicity via their antiinflammatory properties.
source: while M2 macrophages seem to promote tumorigenicity via their antiinflammatory properties (Aras and Zaidi, 2017).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support

claim: A high overall density of macrophages within the NSCLC TME seems to be indicative of a favorable prognosis.
source: A high overall density of macrophages within the NSCLC TME seems to be indicative of a favorable prognosis (Conway et al., 2016; O'Callaghan et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support

claim: A regionally high infiltrate of M2-polarized macrophages in NSCLC tumor islets has a greater association with poor prognosis.
source: As such, a regionally high infiltrate of M2-polarized macrophages in NSCLC tumor islets has a greater association with poor prognosis
evidence: Stated in section I with citation support (Ohri et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2019; Jackute et al., 2018; Sumitomo et al., 2019)

claim: The predominant presence of M1 macrophages indicates increased chances of extended survival and favorable prognosis.
source: while the predominant presence of M1 macrophages indicates increased chances of extended survival and favorable prognosis (Figure 1B; Ohri et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2019; Jackute et al., 2018; Sumitomo et al., 2019).

claim: Macrophage differentiation is increasingly considered to be a spectrum rather than two distinct phenotypes with opposing states of polarization.
source: Nowadays, macrophage differentiation is increasingly considered to be a spectrum rather than two distinct phenotypes with opposing states of polarization.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) reflect an activation state continuum and comprise a large portion of the TME infiltrate in solid tumors.
source: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) reflect an activation state continuum and comprise a large portion of the TME infiltrate in solid tumors (Aras and Zaidi, 2017; Chávez-Galán et al., 2015).

claim: Once at the tumor site, inflammatory monocytes can be stimulated by a range of cytokines to differentiate into TAM phenotype cells.

claim: The functional presence of TAMs is usually associated with the establishment of a tumor-supporting environment, thus relating to poor prognosis and serving as a potential prognostic marker.

claim: While TAMs share some features with the M1/M2 macrophages, they have a distinct transcriptomic profile and are thus considered a separate macrophage subtype.

claim: Dynamic crosstalk between the cells of the tumor and the macrophage infiltrate is associated with tumorigenic processes such as invasion, metastasis, cancer progression, and angiogenesis.
source: Dynamic crosstalk between the cells of the tumor and the macrophage infiltrate is associated with tumorigenic processes such as invasion, metastasis, cancer progression, and angiogenesis (Aras and Zaidi, 2017; Almatroodi et al., 2016).

claim: LC cells maintaining stem cell-like properties via overexpression of Oct4 secrete high levels of macrophage-CSF (M-CSF).

claim: M-CSF promotes TAM polarization toward the M2 phenotype, increasing tumor progression via enhanced cancer cell migration and metastasis.
source: M-CSF promotes TAM polarization toward the M2 phenotype, increasing tumor progression via enhanced cancer cell migration and metastasis (Lu et al., 2020).

claim: Persistent activation of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) in LUAD epithelial cells enhances the pro-inflammatory nature of the TME, recruiting macrophages into the tumor site which in turn favors the development of metastatic foci.
